findings.text: When the captured stack has fewer than three lines, `stackWithoutTwoTopLines` becomes '' and `String(err.stack).endsWith('')` is always true, so the dedup check always passes and the stack is never appended. The old regex left a short stack unchanged, so it was still appended. Example: an `err` with its own stack and a captured stack of `at a\nat b` loses the async call-site frames.

A `dummy.stack` with no newline, such as a bare 'Error' when no frames are captured, now yields '' where the old `replace` returned the string unchanged. `err.stack` is then set to '' (or the append is skipped), which loses the stack.

1.reason: This finding describes the exact reference bug: when the reconstructed stack has fewer than two lines, the sliced suffix becomes the empty string, causing `endsWith('')` to always be true and the stack append to be skipped, which is the same root cause and mechanism as the reference defect.
